Tom — thanks for the note. Long answer short: CFO signoff depends on your internal procurement thresholds, not a Marketplace restriction. From Redwood side the operational activation for co-sell is gated by the buyer acceptance of the private offer and basic accounting evidence; we do not require a separate Redwood exec signature for 12+ months.

Attached is a short workbook with 3 pricing scenarios and a recommended mutual action plan:
- Scenario A: 6-month pilot via private offer (marketplace activation) then 12mo annual commit if pilot metrics met.
- Scenario B: 12-month annual commit standard PO — 10% marketplace discount, co-sell credit eligibility once PO is activated.
- Scenario C: 24-month commit — additional 5% term discount, but requires finance pre-approval for extended billing cadence.

Key asks for procurement:
- Preferred legal signatory name on PO.
- Billing entity (if different from buyer entity).
- If you require invoicing instead of marketplace billing, that typically triggers finance review and may need CFO/FP&A signoff depending on amount.

Vivek / Naomi — can you confirm the discount bands above and whether we can enable co-sell credits at activation (not post-delivery)? Also flag any finance gating for the 24mo scenario.

Hi Tom / Emily — looping in the finance perspective.

Summary of required approvals and evidence for each path:
- Pilot (6mo) via AWS private offer: minimal finance gating. We ask for a signed PO from the buying entity; Redwood invoices via Marketplace settlement — no CFO signature required unless your internal threshold requires it.
- 12mo annual commit: standard Marketplace private offer flow. If billing stays on the marketplace (credit card or marketplace invoice), finance acceptance is routine. If you require external invoicing to Acme AP (off-marketplace invoicing), we need AP contact, EIN, and an invoice terms addendum — amounts > $250k will typically need FP&A / CFO notice.
- 24mo commit / multi-entity billing: must be reviewed by finance. We need to confirm whether the buyer wants a single master PO for multiple operating entities; that introduces legal & tax complexity.

Requested next steps: please confirm which path you prefer and provide the PO signatory name + billing entity. I’m attaching the SOW draft for operational clarity.
